Files and folders in the person's Dropbox.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own Dropbox account once, then allows each app that uses it. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

The redirect URI to register, with your Gateway's address (like `apps.example.com`):

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/dropbox/callback
```

`token_access_type=offline` is what yields a refresh token.

1. Open [dropbox.com](https://www.dropbox.com/developers/apps) and create an OAuth app (also called a client or an integration).
2. Add the redirect URI above.
3. Copy the client ID and client secret. The secret is often shown only once.

Add it to your Gateway. It asks for the client ID and secret:

```bash
everyapp provider add dropbox
```

Or add it in **Manage workspace → Providers**.

### Use it in an app

List the provider's own scopes in the app's `everyapp.config.ts`:

```ts
capabilities: {
  dropbox: { scopes: ["files.metadata.read"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

Use [Dropbox's scopes](https://developers.dropbox.com/oauth-guide). The app calls Dropbox's API with `integrationFetch()`, and the Gateway adds the person's token. A token with more scopes than your apps list is refused.

**Check it worked:** `everyapp provider show dropbox` shows the client as set. Then open an app that lists it and select its **Connect** button.

Something wrong or missing? [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20Dropbox).
